mainTopic: How far a sale reaches: what the word נכסי includes, and how the way boundaries are written in a sale document decides how much land the buyer gets
overview: The amud first finishes a rule about sale wording: if the seller says he is selling his נכסי (property), even houses and slaves are included. Then a new case begins. A sale document lists a long boundary on one side of a field and a short boundary on the other. רב rules that the buyer gets only a strip as wide as the short side. רב כהנא and רב אסי challenge him: why not also give the buyer the triangle (ראש תור) made by joining the end of the short side to the end of the long side? רב is silent. The גמרא then shows a case where רב agrees the triangle is included: the document names two neighbors on one side and only one on the other, even though the seller could easily have named matching neighbors. Next, if one neighbor borders the field on two opposite sides and another neighbor borders the other two, the document must say 'two sides' for each one. Finally, the גמרא asks what the buyer gets if the seller marked only the corners, or only two sides shaped like an L (gamma). That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Selling 'my property' includes houses and slaves
steps.stepSummary: If the seller says he is selling his נכסי, the sale includes even houses and slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he said to him, 'I am selling you my property,' then even his houses and slaves are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a rule about the exact words a seller uses. Saying נכסי ('my property') covers everything, even houses and slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some sale words cover only land. The word נכסי is the widest possible word, so it pulls in buildings and even slaves too. This step closes the discussion about wording before a new case begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves (Canaanite slaves, who count as owned property)

phrases.english: And if he said to him: "my property" —
even houses and slaves are included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion (from before this section) about how wide different sale words are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word נכסי includes all property, even houses and slaves.

steps.title: Long boundary and short boundary: buyer gets only the short width
steps.stepSummary: When the sale document gives one long boundary and one short boundary, רב rules the buyer acquires only a strip as wide as the short side.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller marked out for him one long boundary and one short boundary, רב said: the buyer acquires only the land lined up with the short boundary.
steps.whatsHappening: A new case begins. The two opposite sides of the field in the sale document have different lengths, and רב rules that the buyer gets only what lines up with the shorter side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב assumes the short side shows the real size of what was sold. The long side was just named to help point out which field is meant, not to add land. So anything sticking out past the short side stays with the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: He marked out a boundary (in the sale document)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the long boundary is a mistake. He is saying it was named only to identify the field, not to define how much land was sold.

phrases.english: If he marked out for him one boundary long
and one boundary short —
phrases.notes: These are two opposite sides of the same field, as written in the sale document.

phrases.english: Rav said:
he acquires only what is opposite the short one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצַר לוֹ מֶצֶר אֶחָד אָרוֹךְ וּמֶצֶר אֶחָד קָצָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meaning of sale words to a new case about uneven boundaries.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With one long and one short boundary, the buyer acquires only the width that lines up with the short boundary.

steps.title: Why not give the buyer the triangle too?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי ask why the buyer shouldn't also get the triangle (ראש תור) between the short side's end and the long side's end. רב stays silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: Let him also acquire the triangle-shaped piece! רב was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: Two students challenge רב's ruling. They say the buyer should at least get the triangle formed by drawing a slanted line from the end of the short side to the end of the long side, and רב gives no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their logic: if both boundaries were written, the natural shape is drawn by connecting their ends, which adds a triangle beyond the short-side strip. רב's silence means he did not answer the challenge here. The next step shows where he does agree with them.

keyTerms.meaning: A triangle-shaped strip of land (literally 'head of an ox')

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
But let him acquire up to the triangle!
phrases.notes: Picture a slanted line from the end of the short side to the end of the long side; the extra wedge is the triangle.

phrases.english: Rav was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב וְיִקְנֶה כְּנֶגֶד רֹאשׁ תּוֹר
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the buyer gets only the strip lined up with the short boundary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since both boundaries were written, the buyer should at least get the triangle made by connecting the end of the short side to the end of the long side.

steps.title: When רב agrees the triangle is included
steps.stepSummary: רב admits that if the document names two neighbors on one side and only one on the other, the buyer gets the triangle too, since the seller could have named matching neighbors and did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב agrees in a case where ראובן and שמעון's fields border one side and לוי and יהודה's fields border the other side. Since the seller should have written 'ראובן opposite לוי' or 'שמעון opposite יהודה,' and he didn't, we learn that he meant to give him the triangle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows a case where רב agrees with רב כהנא and רב אסי. When the uneven boundaries come from naming neighbors in a mismatched way, the buyer gets the triangle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the field has two neighbors on each side. If the seller wanted to sell only a straight strip, he could easily have named matching neighbors (ראובן with לוי, or שמעון with יהודה). Since he named ראובן and שמעון on one side but only לוי on the other, his choice shows he meant the slanted line, so the triangle is included.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, we can conclude

steps.whatToRemember: רב's basic rule: with uneven boundaries, the buyer gets only the short-side width. Exception: if the seller could easily have written matching boundaries and chose not to, his wording shows he meant to include the triangle.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a key idea in reading sale documents: what a seller could have written but chose not to write tells us what he meant.

phrases.english: And Rav agrees

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מֶצֶר רְאוּבֵן וְשִׁמְעוֹן מֵחַד גִּיסָא,
phrases.english: where there is a boundary of Reuven and Shimon on one side,
and a boundary of Levi and Yehuda on the other side;
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes the document named ראובן and שמעון on one side but only לוי on the other.

phrases.english: since he should have written for him
'Reuven's opposite Levi's'
or 'Shimon's opposite Yehuda's,'
and he did not write that for him;
conclude from this

phrases.aramaic: כְּנֶגֶד רֹאשׁ תּוֹר הוּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: that it is up to the triangle that he was telling him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַב הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא מֶצֶר רְאוּבֵן וְשִׁמְעוֹן מֵחַד גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב's silence, the גמרא limits his ruling by showing a case where he agrees with the challenge from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the seller names two neighbors on one side and only one on the other, though he could have named matching neighbors, the buyer acquires the triangle as well.

steps.title: Each neighbor's two sides must be spelled out
steps.stepSummary: If ראובן borders the field on the east and west and שמעון on the north and south, the document must state that each borders it on two sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the field is bordered by ראובן's land on the east and west, and by שמעון's land on the north and south, the seller must write for the buyer: 'bordered by ראובן on two sides, and bordered by שמעון on two sides.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another rule about writing boundaries in a sale document. When each neighbor touches the field on two sides, the document must say 'two sides' for each neighbor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the idea from the previous steps: a document that names fewer boundaries can mean a smaller piece of land. If it just named ראובן and שמעון once each, the buyer might get only the part between one side of ראובן and one side of שמעון, not the whole field. Writing 'two sides' for each neighbor closes the field on all four sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Boundary; the neighbor's field that borders the land being sold
He needs to write for him (in the sale document)

phrases.english: If the field is bordered by Reuven on the east and the west,
and bordered by Shimon on the north and the south,
he needs to write for him:
phrases.notes: The seller is writing this in the sale document for the buyer.

phrases.english: "Bordered by Reuven on two sides,
and bordered by Shimon on two sides."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the logic of step 4 (exact wording of neighbors decides how much land is sold) to a field surrounded by two neighbors on opposite sides.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one neighbor borders two opposite sides and another neighbor borders the other two, the document must say 'two sides' for each neighbor to include the whole field.

steps.title: Two questions: only the corners, or an L-shaped boundary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the buyer gets if the seller marked only the corners of the field, or marked only two connecting sides shaped like the letter gamma.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If the seller marked out only the corners for the buyer, what is the law? If he marked the boundaries shaped like a gamma (an L), what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises two related questions about unclear boundary descriptions and leaves them open for now. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First question: if only the corners are marked, does the buyer get just the corners, or the whole field those corners outline? Second question: if only two sides that meet at a right angle are marked, does the buyer get the whole field, or only the triangle closed off by a diagonal line between their ends? Both questions test how far we fill in boundaries the seller did not write out.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים); an open question
Shaped like the Greek letter gamma, an L-shape

steps.confusionAlert: These are questions, not rulings. The גמרא has not yet decided what the buyer gets in either case.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
If he marked out for him the corners, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Does the buyer get just the corners, or everything inside them?

phrases.english: If shaped like a gamma, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Gamma is the Greek letter shaped like an L. He marked only two sides that meet at a corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: סִיֵּים לוֹ אֶת הַקְּרָנוֹת, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clear rules of steps 2 to 5, the גמרא moves to boundary descriptions whose meaning is unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether marking only corners sells only the corners or the whole field, and whether an L-shaped boundary sells the whole field or only the triangle formed by a diagonal between the ends.
